title: Russian 'Mass Strike' Hits Odesa Region, Kills 1, Damages Hotel, Medical Facility and Grain Storage
detail: Russia launched a mass overnight strike on southern Odesa Oblast into September 27 using Shahed-type and Gerbera/Parodiya decoy drones alongside glide bombs, part of a nationwide barrage of 170 attack drones (76 jet-powered), of which Ukrainian air defenses downed or suppressed 147. Odesa Oblast Governor Oleh Kiper said the strike killed one person and injured two, and damaged a residential building, a medical facility, a hotel, a retail store and a grain storage facility; a production facility and warehouse also caught fire. More than 140 State Emergency Service personnel and five National Guard firefighting crews responded. The Kyiv Independent tallied 14 killed and 57 injured nationwide over the preceding 24 hours, with Zaporizhzhia, Sumy and Donetsk oblasts also hit hard.

title: Russian Strikes Kill 3 in Komyshuvakha and Novotavriiske, Zaporizhzhia Oblast
detail: Russian forces struck the villages of Komyshuvakha and Novotavriiske in Zaporizhzhia Oblast overnight into September 27. In Komyshuvakha, shelling killed a man and destroyed one house while damaging several neighboring homes; four people (one woman, three men) were injured. In Novotavriiske, an FPV drone struck a car, killing the man and woman inside. Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration acting head Mykhailo Semikin confirmed the toll. The Kyiv Independent's regional tally put the day's Zaporizhzhia Oblast total at 4 killed and 5 injured as authorities counted additional frontline-area strikes overnight.

title: Russian Drones Strike Kyiv Data Centre Twice, Injuring 3 Including 2 Children
detail: Russian forces struck a data centre in Kyiv twice on the morning of September 27 as part of the nationwide overnight barrage. Three people were injured in the first strike, including two children, and fires broke out in two non-residential buildings in the capital. President Zelensky said Russia had launched more than 2,200 attack drones, roughly 1,650 aerial bombs and 38 missiles against Ukraine over the preceding week, and called on China, India, Brazil, South Africa and other G20 and Global South countries to press Russia to end the war.
